phenomenon.name: The Mothman Prophecies
phenomenon.subcategory: Paranormal nonfiction book and film adaptation

description.summary: The Mothman Prophecies is a 1975 nonfiction book by John Keel investigating the Mothman sightings around Point Pleasant, West Virginia (1966-1967), the December 1967 Silver Bridge collapse, and associated UFO and 'ultraterrestrial' phenomena, later adapted into a 2002 film directed by Mark Pellington.
description.full: The Mothman Prophecies is a 1975 nonfiction book by paranormal author John Keel (Saturday Review Press, 269 pages, ISBN 0-8415-0355-9) chronicling Keel's first-person investigation of the wave of Mothman sightings reported around Point Pleasant, West Virginia between November 1966 and December 1967. The book ties those sightings — beginning with the November 15, 1966 encounter by Roger and Linda Scarberry and Steve and Mary Mallette near the 'TNT area', a former World War II munitions site — to UFO reports, Men in Black encounters and the December 15, 1967 collapse of the Silver Bridge across the Ohio River, in which 46 people died. Keel proposed an 'ultraterrestrial' framework in which intelligences from outside ordinary reality manipulate human perception to generate these phenomena. The book is influential in paranormal literature; a 2002 Skeptical Inquirer article by John C. Sherwood raised accuracy concerns by comparing Keel's contemporaneous correspondence with UFO researcher Gray Barker to his later published account, and the 1971 NTSB investigation determined the Silver Bridge collapse resulted from stress corrosion cracking in a single eyebar (no paranormal cause). The book was loosely adapted into a 2002 feature film directed by Mark Pellington and starring Richard Gere and Laura Linney.

origins.cultural_roots: 1960s-1970s American paranormal and UFO investigation; Keel's earlier work on UFOs and 'ultraterrestrials'.
origins.earliest_accounts: Reporting of the Point Pleasant Mothman flap began in November 1966; Keel investigated through 1967-1968 and published in 1975.
origins.folklore_connections: Connects to Mothman folklore, Silver Bridge memorial culture, Men in Black mythology, and 1970s American UFO/paranormal literature.

timeline.event: Roger and Linda Scarberry and Steve and Mary Mallette report the first widely publicised Mothman encounter near the 'TNT area', Point Pleasant, West Virginia
timeline.significance: Inciting incident of the Mothman flap and of Keel's investigation
timeline.source: Wikipedia: Mothman; Wikipedia: The Mothman Prophecies

timeline.event: The Silver Bridge across the Ohio River collapses, killing 46 people
timeline.significance: Disaster Keel ties to the Mothman flap as a 'prophecy'

timeline.event: NTSB investigation concludes the Silver Bridge collapse was caused by stress corrosion cracking in a suspension chain eyebar
timeline.significance: Mainstream engineering verdict on the disaster (non-paranormal)

timeline.event: John Keel publishes 'The Mothman Prophecies' (Saturday Review Press, ISBN 0-8415-0355-9, 269 pages)
timeline.significance: Founding text of the Mothman literary tradition

timeline.event: Mark Pellington's film adaptation 'The Mothman Prophecies', starring Richard Gere and Laura Linney, releases theatrically (Lakeshore Entertainment / Screen Gems)
John C. Sherwood publishes a Skeptical Inquirer article documenting discrepancies between Keel's contemporaneous correspondence with Gray Barker and his published account
timeline.significance: Skeptical re-examination of the source record

history.modern_era: The book remains in print and is treated as a touchstone of paranormal nonfiction, while critical and skeptical readers note unresolved sourcing concerns. The 2002 film helped popularise Point Pleasant as a destination for paranormal tourism (the town hosts an annual Mothman Festival).

documentary.name: Keel-Barker correspondence (cited by Sherwood, 2002)
documentary.description: Contemporaneous letters between John Keel and UFO researcher Gray Barker, documenting Keel's investigations as they unfolded; cited by John C. Sherwood (Skeptical Inquirer, 2002) as showing discrepancies with Keel's later published account.
documentary.analysis: Used by Sherwood as part of a skeptical re-evaluation of the book's accuracy.

paranormal.name: Keel's 'ultraterrestrial' framework
paranormal.description: John Keel proposed that the Mothman, UFO, and Men-in-Black phenomena around Point Pleasant were manifestations of intelligences from outside ordinary reality manipulating human perception, generating hallucinations and 'prophecy'-like coincidences.
evidence_cited: First-person investigation reported in The Mothman Prophecies (1975)
Reported synchronicities and coincidences during the 1966-1967 flap

skeptical.name: Sherwood discrepancy critique
skeptical.description: John C. Sherwood (Skeptical Inquirer, 2002) compared Keel's contemporaneous correspondence with Gray Barker to the published book and reported discrepancies suggesting Keel's published narrative had been embellished.

skeptical.name: Engineering cause of Silver Bridge collapse
skeptical.description: The 1971 NTSB investigation determined the Silver Bridge collapse was caused by stress corrosion cracking in a single suspension chain eyebar — an engineering, not paranormal, cause.

stories: Roger and Linda Scarberry, Steve and Mary Mallette TNT-area encounter (November 15, 1966)
John Keel's encounters with Men in Black and 'Indrid Cold' as recounted in the book
folklore.beliefs: The Mothman Prophecies has shaped how readers in the English-speaking world understand the relationship between cryptid sightings, prophecy and disaster; skeptical readers treat the book as paranormal nonfiction with documented sourcing concerns.
